name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+13 district lean in northwest Arkansas
Incumbent seeking re-election with no outside spending against him
Markets price Democratic win at just 4%
model.rationale: Womack holds a strong incumbency edge in an R+13 district, with a massive financial advantage and no polls or outside spending suggesting vulnerability. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Steve Womack seeks another term in this solidly Republican northwest Arkansas district, which leans about 13 points to the GOP. He enters the general election with roughly $2.4 million on hand after raising $1.9 million, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised about $120,000 and has under $6,000 available. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and no outside groups are spending on either side. Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the financial gap makes this a comfortable Republican hold, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
